recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Further source edits would be redundant for FHIR-7226 unless Pharmacy makes a new work-group decision to revise the broader MedicationStatement boundary or source wording.
issue_request: FHIR-7226 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request for DSTU1 asking to update the MedicationStatement definition. The old wording identified MedicationStatement by a report from a patient or clinician and the reporter objected that medication-statement data would often come from dispensing-related information, so the distinction based on how it arrived was not good; the accepted resolution proposed a record of medication use as reported by a patient, clinician, or another party.
initial_application: Historical commit e5b1777610 (#7226, 7168) changed the MedicationStatement spreadsheet definition from the old patient-or-clinician report wording to the accepted medication-use-as-reported wording. Related commit 7d50996061 (#7167) then expanded the definition and scope/usage text into the richer MedicationStatement purpose wording that remains in current source.
additional_context: FHIR-7168 was applied in the same historical commit and addressed the closely related question of who can capture or report MedicationStatement information. FHIR-7167, FHIR-5916, and FHIR-5941 are the same 2015 MedicationStatement clarification family; FHIR-5916 and FHIR-5941 already have combined-branch audit commits. Later MedicationStatement history retained the reported-or-derived medication-use semantics and added derivedFrom guidance for links to request, dispense, administration, claims, observations, and questionnaire response information.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active StructureDefinition and introduction already describe MedicationStatement as medication consumed or used by a patient, with information sourced from the patient, patient representative, clinician, prescription bottles, maintained lists, other parties, and derived records, so the current source satisfies FHIR-7226 without reverting to the shorter 2015 sentence.
